title: Meter la pata: colloquial Spanish and idioms
summary: Everyday idioms (meter la pata, tomar el pelo, echar una mano…), the colloquial markers of Spain, intensifiers, and when to leave them out.
content:
## Idioms everyone uses

| idiom | meaning |
|---|---|
| **meter la pata** | put your foot in it |
| **tomar el pelo** a alguien | pull someone's leg |
| **no tener pelos en la lengua** | not mince your words |
| **costar un ojo de la cara** | cost an arm and a leg |
| **echar una mano** | lend a hand |
| **ponerse las pilas** | get your act together |
| **dar la lata** | pester, go on and on |
| **estar como una cabra** | be bonkers |
| **hacer la pelota** | suck up (to someone) |
| **ser uña y carne** | be inseparable |
| **quedarse de piedra** | be stunned |
| **ir al grano** | get to the point |

## Talking like Spain

Small words give speech its rhythm:

- **vale** = OK; **venga** = come on / right then / bye
- **o sea** = I mean, so; **pues nada** = oh well, right then
- **¿sabes?** = you know?; **en plan** = like (young, very informal)
- **tío / tía** = mate, among friends only

## Intensifiers

- **súper** + adjective: *súper fácil*
- **un montón de** = loads of: *un montón de gente*
- **la mar de** = really, ever so: *la mar de contenta*
- **un pelín** = a tiny bit: *un pelín caro*

## Know when to leave them out

Idioms and markers belong to conversation with people you know. In an email to a client, an interview or an essay they sound careless, and some (**estar como una cabra**, **hacer la pelota**) can offend.

| colloquial | neutral | formal |
|---|---|---|
| *Venga, ponte las pilas.* | *Date prisa, por favor.* | *Le ruego que agilice el trámite.* |

vocabulary.meaning: to put your foot in it, to blunder
vocabulary.example: Metí la pata: le pregunté por su novio y lo habían dejado.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I put my foot in it: I asked about her boyfriend and they'd split up.

vocabulary.meaning: to pull someone's leg, to tease
vocabulary.example: ¿Te ha tocado la lotería? Me estás tomando el pelo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: You've won the lottery? You're pulling my leg.

vocabulary.term: no tener pelos en la lengua
vocabulary.example: Mi abuela no tiene pelos en la lengua: te dice lo que piensa.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My grandmother doesn't mince her words: she tells you what she thinks.

vocabulary.term: costar un ojo de la cara
vocabulary.meaning: to cost an arm and a leg
vocabulary.example: Las entradas del concierto costaron un ojo de la cara.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The concert tickets cost an arm and a leg.

vocabulary.example: ¿Me echas una mano con estas cajas?
vocabulary.example_meaning: Can you give me a hand with these boxes?

vocabulary.meaning: to get your act together, to get cracking
vocabulary.example: Si quieres aprobar, ponte las pilas ya.
vocabulary.example_meaning: If you want to pass, get cracking now.

vocabulary.meaning: to pester, to go on and on
vocabulary.example: Los niños llevan toda la tarde dando la lata con el perro.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The kids have been going on about the dog all afternoon.

vocabulary.example: Mi tío está como una cabra: se ha ido a vivir a un barco.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My uncle is bonkers: he's gone to live on a boat.

vocabulary.meaning: to suck up, to butter someone up
vocabulary.example: Deja de hacerle la pelota a la profesora.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Stop sucking up to the teacher.

vocabulary.meaning: to be inseparable, thick as thieves
vocabulary.example: De pequeños, mi hermano y yo éramos uña y carne.
vocabulary.example_meaning: As kids, my brother and I were inseparable.

vocabulary.example: Cuando vi la factura me quedé de piedra.
vocabulary.example_meaning: When I saw the bill I was stunned.

vocabulary.example: No tengo mucho tiempo, así que voy al grano.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I haven't got much time, so I'll get to the point.

vocabulary.example: Tengo un montón de correos sin leer.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I've got loads of unread emails.

vocabulary.example: La cena salió la mar de bien.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Dinner turned out really well.

quiz.prompt: Le dije a Ana que su novio era aburrido… y él estaba detrás de mí. ¡Metí la ___!
quiz.explanation: Meter la pata = to put your foot in it.

quiz.prompt: Este piso cuesta un ojo de la ___.
quiz.explanation: Costar un ojo de la cara = to cost an arm and a leg.
teaches: costar un ojo de la cara

quiz.prompt: What does 'Me estás tomando el pelo' mean?
quiz.explanation: Tomar el pelo = to tease, to pull someone's leg.
hints: Nothing to do with a hairdresser.

quiz.explanation: Echar una mano = to lend a hand.
hints: You'd lend it in English too.

quiz.prompt: Quedan dos semanas para el examen: tienes que ___ las pilas.
quiz.explanation: Ponerse las pilas = to get your act together.

quiz.prompt: Which sentence is for friends only?
quiz.explanation: Venga and tío are colloquial markers used among friends.

quiz.prompt: Mi hermana y su mejor amiga son uña y ___.
quiz.explanation: Ser uña y carne = to be inseparable (like nail and flesh).
hints: What a nail is attached to.

quiz.prompt: In a job interview, which answer is appropriate?
options: Estoy muy motivado para este puesto.
Estoy súper motivado, en plan, un montón.
quiz.correct_answer: Estoy muy motivado para este puesto.
quiz.explanation: Súper, en plan and un montón are colloquial: fine with friends, careless in an interview.

quiz.prompt: Someone who 'no tiene pelos en la lengua'…
quiz.explanation: No tener pelos en la lengua = to say exactly what you think.
teaches: no tener pelos en la lengua

listening.text: No me des la lata, que estoy trabajando.
listening.meaning: Stop pestering me, I'm working.

listening.text: Me quedé de piedra cuando me lo contó.
listening.meaning: I was stunned when she told me.

listening.text: Tu vecino está como una cabra.
listening.meaning: Your neighbour is bonkers.

listening.text: Venga, ve al grano, que tengo prisa.
listening.meaning: Come on, get to the point, I'm in a hurry.

listening.text: Había un montón de gente en el concierto.
listening.meaning: There were loads of people at the concert.

listening.text: Estoy hecho un lío con tanto papeleo.
listening.meaning: I'm in a muddle with so much paperwork.
listening.note: New word: el papeleo = the paperwork.

listening.text: El examen estaba chupado, en plan, facilísimo.
listening.meaning: The exam was a doddle, like, super easy.
listening.note: New word: estar chupado = to be dead easy (colloquial).

listening.text: O sea, que al final no vienes a la boda, ¿no?
listening.meaning: So, in the end you're not coming to the wedding, right?

guide.tip: An idiom used with the wrong person can sound rude. When in doubt, say it plainly.

conversations.title: Office gossip
conversations.scenario: Carla and Lucas, close friends and colleagues, catch up over coffee.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Tío, ¿te has enterado de lo de Raúl?
lines.meaning: Mate, have you heard about Raúl?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: No. Venga, ve al grano.
lines.meaning: No. Come on, get to the point.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Ayer metió la pata en la reunión con los clientes.
lines.meaning: Yesterday he put his foot in it in the meeting with the clients.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¿Raúl? Pero si siempre le hace la pelota a todo el mundo.
lines.meaning: Raúl? But he always sucks up to everybody.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Pues dijo que el producto costaba un ojo de la cara.
lines.meaning: Well, he said the product cost an arm and a leg.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¡Me estás tomando el pelo! ¿Delante de los clientes?
lines.meaning: You're pulling my leg! In front of the clients?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Te lo juro. La jefa se quedó de piedra.
lines.meaning: I swear. The boss was stunned.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Bueno, Raúl nunca ha tenido pelos en la lengua.
lines.meaning: Well, Raúl has never minced his words.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: O sea, que ahora tiene que ponerse las pilas.
lines.meaning: So now he has to get his act together.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Pues nada, habrá que echarle una mano.
lines.meaning: Oh well, we'll have to give him a hand.

bites.title: Body-part idioms
bites.rule: Meter la pata (blunder), tomar el pelo (tease), echar una mano (help), costar un ojo de la cara (be very expensive), no tener pelos en la lengua (be blunt).
bites.example_meaning: Can you give me a hand?

bites.title: Animals and things
bites.rule: Estar como una cabra (be bonkers), ponerse las pilas (get going), dar la lata (pester), quedarse de piedra (be stunned).

bites.title: Vale, venga, o sea
bites.rule: Vale = OK. Venga = come on, right then. O sea = I mean, so. Pues nada = oh well. Tío / tía: friends only.

bites.title: Read the room
bites.rule: Idioms, súper, un montón and en plan are for friends. In emails, interviews and essays, say it plainly.
bites.example: Estoy muy contento con el resultado.
bites.example_meaning: I'm very happy with the result.

Cuesta un ojo de la cara.

The idiom is tomar el pelo.

realm.content:
## Modismos en Eldmark

In the Highgate tavern, the dwarf **metió la pata** with the queen, the bard **nos toma el pelo** with his songs, and the new sword **costó un ojo de la cara**. *¡**Échame una mano** con el barril, que es la mar de pesado!* And the old wizard? **Está como una cabra**, but nobody tells him.

vocabulary.example: El enano metió la pata delante de la reina.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The dwarf put his foot in it in front of the queen.

vocabulary.example: El bardo nos toma el pelo con sus canciones inventadas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The bard pulls our leg with his made-up songs.

vocabulary.term: costar un ojo de la cara
vocabulary.example: La espada élfica me costó un ojo de la cara.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The elven sword cost me an arm and a leg.

vocabulary.example: Échame una mano con el barril, que es la mar de pesado.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Give me a hand with the barrel, it's ever so heavy.

vocabulary.example: El viejo mago está como una cabra.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The old wizard is bonkers.

vocabulary.example: La tabernera no tiene pelos en la lengua.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The innkeeper doesn't mince her words.

vocabulary.example: La cuenta la paga el paladín.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The bill is on the paladin.

vocabulary.example: El orco cuenta chistes malísimos.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The orc tells terrible jokes.

meadowbrook.content:
## Modismos en Meadowbrook

At the seed shop, Leo **nos toma el pelo** with his giant fish, Rosa **no tiene pelos en la lengua**, and Nora and her goat **son uña y carne**. The goat, by the way, **está como una cabra**, literally. *¿Me **echáis una mano** con la cosecha? ¡Venga!*

vocabulary.example: Leo nos toma el pelo con su pez de dos metros.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Leo pulls our leg with his two-metre fish.

vocabulary.term: no tener pelos en la lengua
vocabulary.example: Rosa no tiene pelos en la lengua: si tu tarta está mala, te lo dice.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Rosa doesn't mince her words: if your cake is bad, she tells you.

vocabulary.example: Nora y su cabra son uña y carne.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Nora and her goat are inseparable.

vocabulary.example: La cabra de Nora está como una cabra, literalmente.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Nora's goat is bonkers, literally.

vocabulary.example: ¿Me echáis una mano con la cosecha?
vocabulary.example_meaning: Will you give me a hand with the harvest?

vocabulary.example: En la tienda de Rosa se oye todo el cotilleo del pueblo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: At Rosa's shop you hear all the town gossip.

vocabulary.example: Leo presume de sus peces todo el día.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Leo brags about his fish all day.

vocabulary.example: No piques el anzuelo: Leo te está tomando el pelo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Don't take the bait: Leo is pulling your leg.

conversations.title: The fish that got bigger
conversations.scenario: Leo boasts about a fish to Nora at the seed shop.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Nora, ayer pesqué un pez de dos metros.
lines.meaning: Nora, yesterday I caught a two-metre fish.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Venga ya, Leo. Me estás tomando el pelo.
lines.meaning: Oh come on, Leo. You're pulling my leg.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Te lo juro. Me quedé de piedra al verlo.
lines.meaning: I swear. I was stunned when I saw it.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¿Y dónde está ese pez?
lines.meaning: And where's this fish?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Pues… se escapó. Rompió el anzuelo.
lines.meaning: Well… it got away. It broke the hook.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Claro. Siempre presumes y nunca hay pruebas.
lines.meaning: Of course. You always brag and there's never any proof.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Vale, vale. Medía un metro. O sea, casi.
lines.meaning: OK, OK. It was one metre. I mean, nearly.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¿Un metro o un palmo? Ve al grano.
lines.meaning: One metre or a hand's span? Get to the point.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Pues nada, era una sardina. Pero la mar de bonita.
lines.meaning: Oh well, it was a sardine. But ever so pretty.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Anda, échame una mano con las calabazas y deja de presumir.
lines.meaning: Go on, give me a hand with the pumpkins and stop showing off.

rustwake.content:
## Modismos en el páramo

The gardener robot is learning slang and takes everything literally. Leo says *te estoy tomando el pelo* and the robot looks for hair. Marta says *ponte las pilas* and it opens its battery hatch. *Pues nada*, says Ruiz: *este robot **está como una cabra***. The robot searches for a goat.

vocabulary.example: Leo le toma el pelo al robot todos los días.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Leo pulls the robot's leg every day.

vocabulary.example: Ponte las pilas, robot, que hay que regar el huerto.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Get cracking, robot, the garden needs watering.

vocabulary.example: Ruiz dice que el robot está como una cabra.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Ruiz says the robot is bonkers.

vocabulary.example: El robot nos da la lata con sus preguntas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The robot pesters us with its questions.

vocabulary.example: El robot se quedó de piedra: no entendía nada.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The robot froze: it didn't understand a thing.

vocabulary.example: El robot está aprendiendo la jerga del páramo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The robot is learning wasteland slang.

vocabulary.example: Para el robot, todo es literal.
vocabulary.example_meaning: For the robot, everything is literal.

vocabulary.example: Con tanto modismo se le quema un circuito.
vocabulary.example_meaning: With so many idioms, a circuit burns out on it.

bites.title: El robot literal
bites.rule: Idioms never mean what their words say. Tomar el pelo isn't about hair, ponerse las pilas isn't about batteries, estar como una cabra isn't about goats.

listening.text: El robot aprende la jerga del páramo.
listening.meaning: The robot is learning wasteland slang.

listening.text: Para el robot, cada modismo es literal.
listening.meaning: For the robot, every idiom is literal.

listening.text: El robot por fin se puso las pilas.
listening.meaning: The robot finally got its act together.

listening.text: Se le quemó un circuito.
listening.meaning: One of its circuits burnt out.
listening.note: New word: el circuito = the circuit.

listening.text: Leo le toma el pelo.
listening.meaning: Leo pulls its leg.
